gene.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 8
gene.function: Regulator subunit of pancreatic ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP), playing a major role in the regulation of insulin release. In pancreatic cells, it forms KATP channels with KCNJ11; KCNJ11 forms the channel pore while ABCC8 is required for activation and regulation.

gene.name: alanine--glyoxylate aminotransferase
gene.function: Peroxisomal aminotransferase that catalyzes the transamination of glyoxylate to glycine and contributes to the glyoxylate detoxification. Also catalyzes the transamination between L-serine and pyruvate and contributes to gluconeogenesis from the L-serine metabolism.

gene.name: aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B
gene.function: Catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of a wide variety of carbonyl-containing compounds to their corresponding alcohols. Displays enzymatic activity towards endogenous metabolites such as aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, ketones, monosaccharides, bile acids and xenobiotics substrates. It catalyzes the reduction of glucose to sorbitol, the first step of the polyol pathway, an alternative route of glucose metabolism that converts glucose to fructose. This pathway becomes highly active under elevated glucose levels, such as during hyperglycemia. Reduces steroids and their derivatives and prostaglandins. Displays low enzymatic activity toward all-trans-retinal, 9-cis-retinal, and 13-cis- retinal. Catalyzes the reduction of diverse phospholipid aldehydes such as 1-palmitoyl-2- (5-oxovaleroyl)-sn -glycero-3-phosphoethanolamin (POVPC) and related phospholipid aldehydes that are generated from the oxydation of phosphotidylcholine and phosphatdyleethanolamides. Plays a role in detoxifying dietary and lipid-derived unsaturated carbonyls, such as crotonaldehyde, 4-hydroxynonenal, trans-2-hexenal, trans-2,4-hexadienal and their glutathione-conjugates carbonyls (GS- carbonyls).

gene.name: ALG1 chitobiosyldiphosphodolichol beta-mannosyltransferase
gene.function: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation. The assembly of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides begins on the cytosolic side of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and finishes in its lumen. The sequential addition of sugars to dolichol pyrophosphate produces dolichol-linked oligosaccharides containing fourteen sugars, including two GlcNAcs, nine mannoses and three glucoses. Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins by oligosaccharyltransferases. Catalyzes, on the cytoplasmic face of the endoplasmic reticulum, the addition of the first mannose residues to the dolichol-linked oligosaccharide chain, to produce Man1GlcNAc(2)-PP- dolichol core oligosaccharide. Man1GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol is a substrate for ALG2, the following enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway.

gene.name: ALG12 alpha-1,6-mannosyltransferase
gene.function: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation. The assembly of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides begins on the cytosolic side of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and finishes in its lumen. The sequential addition of sugars to dolichol pyrophosphate produces dolichol-linked oligosaccharides containing fourteen sugars, including two GlcNAcs, nine mannoses and three glucoses. Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins by oligosaccharyltransferases. In the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum, adds the eighth mannose residue in an alpha-1,6 linkage onto Man(7)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol to produce Man(8)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol.

gene.name: ALG9 alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase
gene.function: Mannosyltransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation. The assembly of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides begins on the cytosolic side of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and finishes in its lumen. The sequential addition of sugars to dolichol pyrophosphate produces dolichol-linked oligosaccharides containing fourteen sugars, including two GlcNAcs, nine mannoses and three glucoses. Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins by oligosaccharyltransferases. In the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum, catalyzes the addition of the seventh and ninth alpha-1,2-linked mannose residues to Man(6)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol and Man(8)GlcNAc(2)-PP- dolichol respectively.

gene.name: attractin
gene.function: Involved in the initial immune cell clustering during inflammatory response and may regulate chemotactic activity of chemokines. May play a role in melanocortin signaling pathways that regulate energy homeostasis and hair color. Low-affinity receptor for agouti (By similarity). Has a critical role in normal myelination in the central nervous system (By similarity).

gene.name: BCL2 apoptosis regulator
gene.function: Suppresses apoptosis in a variety of cell systems including factor-dependent lymphohematopoietic and neural cells. Regulates cell death by controlling the mitochondrial membrane permeability. Appears to function in a feedback loop system with caspases. Inhibits caspase activity either by preventing the release of cytochrome c from the mitochondria and/or by binding to the apoptosis-activating factor (APAF-1). Also acts as an inhibitor of autophagy: interacts with BECN1 and AMBRA1 during non-starvation conditions and inhibits their autophagy function. May attenuate inflammation by impairing NLRP1- inflammasome activation, hence CASP1 activation and IL1B release.

gene.name: bisphosphoglycerate mutase
gene.function: Plays a major role in regulating hemoglobin oxygen affinity by controlling the levels of its allosteric effector 2,3- bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG). Also exhibits mutase (EC 5.4.2.11) activity. .

gene.name: complement C3
gene.function: Precursor of non-enzymatic components of the classical, alternative, lectin and GZMK complement pathways, which consist in a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens and signaling that strengthens the adaptive immune system.

gene.name: complement C4A (Chido/Rodgers blood group)
gene.function: Precursor of non-enzymatic components of the classical, lectin and GZMK complement pathways, which consist in a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens and signaling that strengthens the adaptive immune system.

gene.name: calcium regulated heat stable protein 1
gene.function: Binds mRNA and regulates the stability of target mRNA. Binds single-stranded DNA (in vitro).

gene.name: cystathionine beta-synthase
gene.function: Hydro-lyase catalyzing the first step of the transsulfuration pathway, where the hydroxyl group of L-serine is displaced by L- homocysteine in a beta-replacement reaction to form L-cystathionine, the precursor of L-cysteine. This catabolic route allows the elimination of L-methionine and the toxic metabolite L-homocysteine. Also involved in the production of hydrogen sulfide, a gasotransmitter with signaling and cytoprotective effects on neurons (By similarity).

gene.name: carbohydrate sulfotransferase 3
gene.function: Sulfotransferase that utilizes 3'-phospho-5'-adenylyl sulfate (PAPS) as sulfonate donor to catalyze the transfer of sulfate to position 6 of the N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of chondroitin. Chondroitin sulfate constitutes the predominant proteoglycan present in cartilage and is distributed on the surfaces of many cells and extracellular matrices. Catalyzes with a lower efficiency the sulfation of Gal residues of keratan sulfate, another glycosaminoglycan. Can also catalyze the sulfation of the Gal residues in sialyl N-acetyllactosamine (sialyl LacNAc) oligosaccharides (By similarity). May play a role in the maintenance of naive T-lymphocytes in the spleen (By similarity).

gene.name: dolichyl-phosphate N-acetylglucosaminephosphotransferase 1
gene.function: UDP-N-acetylglucosamine--dolichyl-phosphate N- acetylglucosaminephosphotransferase that operates in the biosynthetic pathway of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides, the glycan precursors employed in protein asparagine (N)-glycosylation. The assembly of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides begins on the cytosolic side of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and finishes in its lumen. The sequential addition of sugars to dolichol pyrophosphate produces dolichol-linked oligosaccharides containing fourteen sugars, including two GlcNAcs, nine mannoses and three glucoses. Once assembled, the oligosaccharide is transferred from the lipid to nascent proteins by oligosaccharyltransferases. Catalyzes the initial step of dolichol- linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis, transferring GlcNAc-1-P from cytosolic UDP-GlcNAc onto the carrier lipid dolichyl phosphate (P- dolichol), yielding GlcNAc-P-P-dolichol embedded in the cytoplasmic leaflet of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.

gene.name: coagulation factor XII
gene.function: Factor XII is a serum glycoprotein that participates in the initiation of blood coagulation, fibrinolysis, and the generation of bradykinin and angiotensin. Prekallikrein is cleaved by factor XII to form kallikrein, which then cleaves factor XII first to alpha-factor XIIa and then trypsin cleaves it to beta-factor XIIa. Alpha-factor XIIa activates factor XI to factor XIa.

gene.name: glucosylceramidase beta 1
gene.function: Glucosylceramidase that catalyzes, within the lysosomal compartment, the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers (such as beta- D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) into free ceramides (such as N-acylsphing-4-enine) and glucose. Plays a central role in the degradation of complex lipids and the turnover of cellular membranes. Through the production of ceramides, participates in the PKC-activated salvage pathway of ceramide formation. Catalyzes the glucosylation of cholesterol, through a transglucosylation reaction where glucose is transferred from GlcCer to cholesterol. GlcCer containing mono-unsaturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-(9Z-octadecenoyl)-sphing-4-enine) are preferred as glucose donors for cholesterol glucosylation when compared with GlcCer containing same chain length of saturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-octadecanoyl-sphing-4-enine). Under specific conditions, may alternatively catalyze the reverse reaction, transferring glucose from cholesteryl 3-beta-D-glucoside to ceramide (Probable). Can also hydrolyze cholesteryl 3-beta-D- glucoside producing glucose and cholesterol. Catalyzes the hydrolysis of galactosylceramides/GalCers (such as beta-D-galactosyl-(1<->1')-N- acylsphing-4-enine), as well as the transfer of galactose between GalCers and cholesterol in vitro, but with lower activity than with GlcCers. Contrary to GlcCer and GalCer, xylosylceramide/XylCer (such as beta-D-xyosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4- enine) is not a good substrate for hydrolysis, however it is a good xylose donor for transxylosylation activity to form cholesteryl 3-beta- D-xyloside. Can also metabolize plant glycosyl phytosterols such as glucosylstigmasterol.

gene.name: glutamine--fructose-6-phosphate transaminase 1
gene.function: Rate-limiting enzyme of the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) that catalyzes the formation of glucosamine-6-phosphate from fructose-6-phosphate and glutamine, thereby controlling the flux of glucose into this pathway. Inhibited by UDP-N-acetylglucosamine (UDP-GlcNAc) through a feedback loop. Fine-tunes the metabolic fluctuations of UDP-GlcNAc and its impacts on hyaluronan synthesis during tissue remodeling. Via control of the HPB, regulates the availability of precursors for N- and O-linked protein glycosylation and modulates peripheral clock oscillation (By similarity).

gene.name: hyaluronan and proteoglycan link protein 1
gene.function: Stabilizes the aggregates of proteoglycan monomers with hyaluronic acid in the extracellular cartilage matrix.

gene.name: lysosome associated membrane protein 1
gene.function: Lysosomal membrane glycoprotein which plays an important role in lysosome biogenesis, lysosomal pH regulation, autophagy and cholesterol homeostasis. Acts as an important regulator of lysosomal lumen pH regulation by acting as a direct inhibitor of the proton channel TMEM175, facilitating lysosomal acidification for optimal hydrolase activity. Also plays an important role in NK-cells cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, participates in cytotoxic granule movement to the cell surface and perforin trafficking to the lytic granule. In addition, protects NK-cells from degranulation-associated damage induced by their own cytotoxic granule content. Presents carbohydrate ligands to selectins.

gene.name: lysosome associated membrane protein 2
gene.function: Lysosomal membrane glycoprotein which plays an important role in lysosome biogenesis, lysosomal pH regulation and autophagy. Acts as an important regulator of lysosomal lumen pH regulation by acting as a direct inhibitor of the proton channel TMEM175, facilitating lysosomal acidification for optimal hydrolase activity. Plays an important role in chaperone-mediated autophagy, a process that mediates lysosomal degradation of proteins in response to various stresses and as part of the normal turnover of proteins with a long biological half-live. Functions by binding target proteins, such as GAPDH, GPX4, NLRP3 and MLLT11, and targeting them for lysosomal degradation. In the chaperone-mediated autophagy, acts downstream of chaperones, such as HSPA8/HSC70, which recognize and bind substrate proteins and mediate their recruitment to lysosomes, where target proteins bind LAMP2. Plays a role in lysosomal protein degradation in response to starvation (By similarity). Required for the fusion of autophagosomes with lysosomes during autophagy. Cells that lack LAMP2 express normal levels of VAMP8, but fail to accumulate STX17 on autophagosomes, which is the most likely explanation for the lack of fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes. Required for normal degradation of the contents of autophagosomes. Required for efficient MHC class II-mediated presentation of exogenous antigens via its function in lysosomal protein degradation; antigenic peptides generated by proteases in the endosomal/lysosomal compartment are captured by nascent MHC II subunits. Is not required for efficient MHC class II-mediated presentation of endogenous antigens.

gene.name: matrix metallopeptidase 2
gene.function: Ubiquitinous metalloproteinase that is involved in diverse functions such as remodeling of the vasculature, angiogenesis, tissue repair, tumor invasion, inflammation, and atherosclerotic plaque rupture. As well as degrading extracellular matrix proteins, can also act on several nonmatrix proteins such as big endothelial 1 and beta- type CGRP promoting vasoconstriction. Also cleaves KISS at a Gly-|-Leu bond. Appears to have a role in myocardial cell death pathways. Contributes to myocardial oxidative stress by regulating the activity of GSK3beta. Cleaves GSK3beta in vitro. Involved in the formation of the fibrovascular tissues in association with MMP14.

gene.name: mannose phosphate isomerase
gene.function: Isomerase that catalyzes the interconversion of fructose-6-P and mannose-6-P and has a critical role in the supply of D-mannose derivatives required for many eukaryotic glycosylation reactions.

gene.name: phenylalanine hydroxylase
gene.function: Catalyzes the hydroxylation of L-phenylalanine to L-tyrosine. .

gene.name: phosphoglucomutase 1
gene.function: Catalyzes the reversible isomerization of alpha-D-glucose 1- phosphate to alpha-D-glucose 6-phosphate. The mechanism proceeds via the intermediate compound alpha-D-glucose 1,6-bisphosphate (Probable). This enzyme participates in both the breakdown and synthesis of glucose.

gene.name: phosphoglucomutase 2
gene.function: Catalyzes the conversion of the nucleoside breakdown products ribose-1-phosphate and deoxyribose-1-phosphate to the corresponding 5- phosphopentoses. Catalyzes the reversible isomerization of alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate to alpha-D-glucose 6- phosphate but with a lower catalytic efficiency. The mechanism proceeds via the intermediate compound alpha-D-glucose 1,6- bisphosphate. In vitro, also has a low glucose 1,6- bisphosphate synthase activity which is most probably not physiologically relevant. .

gene.name: phosphoglucomutase 2 like 1
gene.function: Glucose 1,6-bisphosphate synthase using 1,3- bisphosphoglycerate as a phosphate donor and a series of 1-phosphate sugars, including glucose 1-phosphate, mannose 1-phosphate, ribose 1- phosphate and deoxyribose 1-phosphate, as acceptors. In vitro, also exhibits very low phosphopentomutase and phosphoglucomutase activity which are most probably not physiologically relevant.

gene.name: PTEN induced kinase 1
gene.function: Serine/threonine-protein kinase which acts as a sensor of mitochondrial damage and protects against mitochondrial dysfunction during cellular stress. It phosphorylates mitochondrial proteins to coordinate mitochondrial quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components. In healthy mitochondria, PINK1 is translocated across the mitochondrial outer membrane (MOM) via the translocase of the outer membrane (TOM) complex, and inserted into the mitochondrial inner membrane (MIM) via the translocase of the inner membrane (TIM23) complex where it is cleaved and released into the cytosol. Depending on the severity of mitochondrial damage, activity ranges from preventing apoptosis and stimulating mitochondrial biogenesis to eliminating severely damaged mitochondria via PINK1-PRKN- dependent mitophagy. When cellular stress results in irreversible mitochondrial damage, PINK1 accumulates at the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) where it phosphorylates pre-existing polyubiquitin chains at 'Ser-65', recruits PRKN from the cytosol to the OMM and activates PRKN by phosphorylation at 'Ser-65'; activated PRKN then ubiquitinates VDAC1 and other OMM proteins to initiate mitophagy. The PINK1-PRKN pathway also promotes fission of damaged mitochondria through phosphorylation and PRKN- dependent degradation of mitochondrial proteins involved in fission such as MFN2. This prevents the refusion of unhealthy mitochondria with the mitochondrial network or initiates mitochondrial fragmentation facilitating their later engulfment by autophagosomes. Also promotes mitochondrial fission independently of PRKN and ATG7- mediated mitophagy, via the phosphorylation and activation of DNM1L. Regulates motility of damaged mitochondria by promoting the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of MIRO1 and MIRO2; in motor neurons, this likely inhibits mitochondrial intracellular anterograde transport along the axons which probably increases the chance of the mitochondria undergoing mitophagy in the soma. Required for ubiquinone reduction by mitochondrial complex I by mediating phosphorylation of complex I subunit NDUFA10 (By similarity). Phosphorylates LETM1, positively regulating its mitochondrial calcium transport activity.

gene.name: phosphomannomutase 1
gene.function: Involved in the synthesis of the GDP-mannose and dolichol- phosphate-mannose required for a number of critical mannosyl transfer reactions. In addition, may be responsible for the degradation of glucose-1,6-bisphosphate in ischemic brain. .

gene.name: phosphomannomutase 2
gene.function: Involved in the synthesis of the GDP-mannose and dolichol- phosphate-mannose required for a number of critical mannosyl transfer reactions. .

gene.name: parkin RBR E3 ubiquitin protein ligase
gene.function: Functions within a multiprotein E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, catalyzing the covalent attachment of ubiquitin moieties onto substrate proteins. Substrates include SYT11 and VDAC1. Other substrates are BCL2, CCNE1, GPR37, RHOT1/MIRO1, MFN1, MFN2, STUB1, SNCAIP, SEPTIN5, TOMM20, USP30, ZNF746, MIRO1 and AIMP2. Mediates monoubiquitination as well as 'Lys-6', 'Lys-11', 'Lys-48'-linked and 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitination of substrates depending on the context. Participates in the removal and/or detoxification of abnormally folded or damaged protein by mediating 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitination of misfolded proteins such as PARK7: 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitinated misfolded proteins are then recognized by HDAC6, leading to their recruitment to aggresomes, followed by degradation. Mediates 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitination of a 22 kDa O-linked glycosylated isoform of SNCAIP, possibly playing a role in Lewy-body formation. Mediates monoubiquitination of BCL2, thereby acting as a positive regulator of autophagy. Protects against mitochondrial dysfunction during cellular stress, by acting downstream of PINK1 to coordinate mitochondrial quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components. Depending on the severity of mitochondrial damage and/or dysfunction, activity ranges from preventing apoptosis and stimulating mitochondrial biogenesis to regulating mitochondrial dynamics and eliminating severely damaged mitochondria via mitophagy. Activation and recruitment onto the outer membrane of damaged/dysfunctional mitochondria (OMM) requires PINK1-mediated phosphorylation of both PRKN and ubiquitin. After mitochondrial damage, functions with PINK1 to mediate the decision between mitophagy or preventing apoptosis by inducing either the poly- or monoubiquitination of VDAC1, respectively; polyubiquitination of VDAC1 promotes mitophagy, while monoubiquitination of VDAC1 decreases mitochondrial calcium influx which ultimately inhibits apoptosis. When cellular stress results in irreversible mitochondrial damage, promotes the autophagic degradation of dysfunctional depolarized mitochondria (mitophagy) by promoting the ubiquitination of mitochondrial proteins such as TOMM20, RHOT1/MIRO1, MFN1 and USP30. Preferentially assembles 'Lys-6'-, 'Lys-11'- and 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitin chains, leading to mitophagy. The PINK1-PRKN pathway also promotes fission of damaged mitochondria by PINK1-mediated phosphorylation which promotes the PRKN-dependent degradation of mitochondrial proteins involved in fission such as MFN2. This prevents the refusion of unhealthy mitochondria with the mitochondrial network or initiates mitochondrial fragmentation facilitating their later engulfment by autophagosomes. Regulates motility of damaged mitochondria via the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of MIRO1 and MIRO2; in motor neurons, this likely inhibits mitochondrial intracellular anterograde transport along the axons which probably increases the chance of the mitochondria undergoing mitophagy in the soma. Involved in mitochondrial biogenesis via the 'Lys-48'-linked polyubiquitination of transcriptional repressor ZNF746/PARIS which leads to its subsequent proteasomal degradation and allows activation of the transcription factor PPARGC1A. Limits the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Regulates cyclin-E during neuronal apoptosis. In collaboration with CHPF isoform 2, may enhance cell viability and protect cells from oxidative stress. Independently of its ubiquitin ligase activity, protects from apoptosis by the transcriptional repression of p53/TP53. May protect neurons against alpha synuclein toxicity, proteasomal dysfunction, GPR37 accumulation, and kainate-induced excitotoxicity. May play a role in controlling neurotransmitter trafficking at the presynaptic terminal and in calcium-dependent exocytosis. May represent a tumor suppressor gene.

gene.name: solute carrier family 2 member 1
gene.function: Facilitative glucose transporter, which is responsible for constitutive or basal glucose uptake. Has a very broad substrate specificity; can transport a wide range of aldoses including both pentoses and hexoses. Most important energy carrier of the brain: present at the blood-brain barrier and assures the energy- independent, facilitative transport of glucose into the brain. In association with BSG and NXNL1, promotes retinal cone survival by increasing glucose uptake into photoreceptors (By similarity). Required for mesendoderm differentiation (By similarity).

gene.name: signal transducer and activator of transcription 3
gene.function: Signal transducer and transcription activator that mediates cellular responses to interleukins, KITLG/SCF, LEP and other growth factors. Once activated, recruits coactivators, such as NCOA1 or MED1, to the promoter region of the target gene. May mediate cellular responses to activated FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3 and FGFR4. Upon activation of IL6ST/gp130 signaling by interleukin-6 (IL6), binds to the IL6-responsive elements identified in the promoters of various acute-phase protein genes. Activated by IL31 through IL31RA. Acts as a regulator of inflammatory response by regulating differentiation of naive CD4(+) T-cells into T-helper Th17 or regulatory T-cells (Treg): acetylation promotes its transcription activity and cell differentiation while deacetylation and oxidation of lysine residues by LOXL3 inhibits differentiation. Involved in cell cycle regulation by inducing the expression of key genes for the progression from G1 to S phase, such as CCND1. Mediates the effects of LEP on melanocortin production, body energy homeostasis and lactation (By similarity). May play an apoptotic role by transactivating BIRC5 expression under LEP activation. Cytoplasmic STAT3 represses macroautophagy by inhibiting EIF2AK2/PKR activity. Plays a crucial role in basal beta cell functions, such as regulation of insulin secretion (By similarity). Following JAK/STAT signaling activation and as part of a complex with NFATC3 and NFATC4, binds to the alpha-beta E4 promoter region of CRYAB and activates transcription in cardiomyocytes (By similarity). Involved in the oncostatin-M-mediated signaling pathway through both type I OSM receptor complex (heterodimers composed of LIFR and IL6ST) and type II OSM receptor complex (heterodimers composed of OSMR and IL6ST).

gene.name: tumor protein p53
gene.function: Multifunctional transcription factor that induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis upon binding to its target DNA sequence. Acts as a tumor suppressor in many tumor types; induces growth arrest or apoptosis depending on the physiological circumstances and cell type. Negatively regulates cell division by controlling expression of a set of genes required for this process. One of the activated genes is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases. Apoptosis induction seems to be mediated either by stimulation of BAX and FAS antigen expression, or by repression of Bcl-2 expression. Its pro-apoptotic activity is activated via its interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2. However, this activity is inhibited when the interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2 is displaced by PPP1R13L/iASPP. In cooperation with mitochondrial PPIF is involved in activating oxidative stress-induced necrosis; the function is largely independent of transcription. Induces the transcription of long intergenic non-coding RNA p21 (lincRNA-p21) and lincRNA-Mkln1. LincRNA-p21 participates in TP53-dependent transcriptional repression leading to apoptosis and seems to have an effect on cell-cycle regulation. Implicated in Notch signaling cross-over. Prevents CDK7 kinase activity when associated to CAK complex in response to DNA damage, thus stopping cell cycle progression. Isoform 2 enhances the transactivation activity of isoform 1 from some but not all TP53-inducible promoters. Isoform 4 suppresses transactivation activity and impairs growth suppression mediated by isoform 1. Isoform 7 inhibits isoform 1-mediated apoptosis. Regulates the circadian clock by repressing CLOCK-BMAL1-mediated transcriptional activation of PER2.

gene.name: vacuolar protein sorting 4 homolog A
gene.function: Involved in late steps of the endosomal multivesicular bodies (MVB) pathway. Recognizes membrane-associated ESCRT-III assemblies and catalyzes their disassembly, possibly in combination with membrane fission. Redistributes the ESCRT-III components to the cytoplasm for further rounds of MVB sorting. MVBs contain intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) that are generated by invagination and scission from the limiting membrane of the endosome and mostly are delivered to lysosomes enabling degradation of membrane proteins, such as stimulated growth factor receptors, lysosomal enzymes and lipids. It is required for proper accomplishment of various processes including the regulation of endosome size, primary cilium organization, mitotic spindle organization, chromosome segregation, and nuclear envelope sealing and spindle disassembly during anaphase. Involved in cytokinesis: retained at the midbody by ZFYVE19/ANCHR and CHMP4C until abscission checkpoint signaling is terminated at late cytokinesis. It is then released following dephosphorylation of CHMP4C, leading to abscission. VPS4A/B are required for the exosomal release of SDCBP, CD63 and syndecan. Critical for normal erythroblast cytokinesis and correct erythropoiesis.

gaps.rationale: PMM2-CDG is caused by deficient phosphomannomutase activity, whereas phosphomannomutase/phosphoglucomutase inhibitors would be expected to further inhibit the same central pathway rather than correct it.
gaps.caveat: The cited evidence only identifies PMM/PGM inhibition as a general drug-development strategy and provides no safety, efficacy, or tissue-specific rationale for this multisystem disorder.
gaps.experiment: Before any therapeutic efficacy study, test candidate inhibitors in patient-derived fibroblasts for PMM2 activity and N-glycosylation to determine whether they worsen rather than rescue the biochemical defect.

papers.title: AZATAX: Acetazolamide safety and efficacy in cerebellar syndrome in PMM2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: The AZATAX clinical trial found that acetazolamide was generally well tolerated in 24 patients with PMM2-CDG and improved motor cerebellar syndrome, with significant improvements in ICARS, NPCRS, and PATA test scores. The randomized withdrawal phase showed worsening of ICARS after acetazolamide withdrawal, while effects on stroke-like episodes and long-term kidney function remain uncertain.
papers.why: A phase II trial found acetazolamide generally well tolerated and associated with improvement in motor cerebellar syndrome in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Repurposing the aldose reductase inhibitor and diabetic neuropathy drug epalrestat for the congenital disorder of glycosylation PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: A cross-species drug-repurposing screen identified epalrestat as a small-molecule activator that increased PMM2 enzymatic activity in a hypomorphic pmm-2 worm model and in four PMM2-CDG patient fibroblast genotypes carrying R141H. The effect was post-translational rather than caused by increased PMM2 protein abundance, and the proposed polyol-pathway mechanism and clinical benefit in PMM2-CDG patients remain unconfirmed.
papers.why: Identified epalrestat as an orally available small molecule that increased mutant PMM2 activity by 30–400% across four patient fibroblast lines.

papers.title: 29 French adult patients with PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation: outcome of the classical pediatric phenotype and depiction of a late-onset phenotype.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 29 French adolescent and adult patients with molecularly confirmed PMM2-CDG, stable cerebellar atrophy was universal, while motor disability, peripheral neuropathy, epilepsy, coagulation abnormalities, thrombosis, retinitis pigmentosa, skeletal disease, growth retardation, and primary ovarian insufficiency characterized long-term outcomes. The paper also defines a screening-to-confirmation diagnostic pathway and supports systematic adult neurological, ophthalmological, laboratory, bone-density, rehabilitation, and thrombosis monitoring.
papers.why: This longitudinal cohort provides natural-history data and clinically relevant adult outcomes for PMM2-CDG, including complications and late-onset phenotypes.

papers.title: Phosphomannomutase deficiency (PMM2-CDG): ataxia and cerebellar assessment.
papers.summary: In 13 children and adolescents with genetically confirmed PMM2-CDG, the International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) showed high inter-rater reliability and correlated with multisystem disease severity, intelligence quotient, and MRI-based midsagittal vermis size. The study supports ICARS as an outcome measure for cerebellar dysfunction, while MRI measurements and NPCRS provided complementary but less specific assessments and genotype–phenotype conclusions were limited by the small sample.
papers.why: The study validates the ICARS as a reproducible clinical outcome measure and relates cerebellar function to MRI and cognitive measures in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: A zebrafish model of PMM2-CDG reveals altered neurogenesis and a substrate-accumulation mechanism for N-linked glycosylation deficiency.
papers.summary: A splice-morpholino zebrafish model of PMM2-CDG recapitulates craniofacial, motility, neurogenesis, and N-glycosylation defects and directly demonstrates reduced lipid-linked oligosaccharides. The study identifies accumulation of mannose-6-phosphate, rather than only depletion of mannose-1-phosphate, as a major contributor to LLO hydrolysis and proposes partial metabolic-flux intervention as a therapeutic strategy.
papers.why: The study created the first PMM2-CDG zebrafish model and showed experimentally that suppressing M6P synthesis normalizes selected disease phenotypes and abnormal oligosaccharide cleavage.

papers.title: A mouse model of a human congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by loss of PMM2.
papers.summary: The study developed the viable Pmm2R137H/F115L knock-in mouse as a model of PMM2-CDG and showed that it reproduces major biochemical, growth, skeletal, ocular, renal, cardiac, and hepatic abnormalities. Patient-derived fibroblasts confirmed reduced PMM2-pathway activity, while wild-type PMM2 overexpression restored pathway metabolites and glycoprotein expression; mannose supplementation did not improve survival of the compound-heterozygous mice.
papers.why: This study provides a patient-relevant mouse and cellular model, glycosylation biomarkers, functional assays, and a gene-replacement rescue strategy directly for PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Glycomic Characterization of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Derived from a Patient Suffering from Phosphomannomutase 2 Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: Patient-derived PMM2-iPSC-C3 cells reproduced reduced phosphomannomutase activity and moderate N-glycosylation defects while retaining pluripotency and differentiation capacity. PMM2 knockdown produced stepwise stronger biochemical defects, and mannose supplementation increased cell-surface mannosylation, establishing a human stem-cell platform for studying PMM2-CDG and related glycosylation mechanisms.
papers.why: Generated a pluripotent patient-derived cellular model that reproduced reduced PMM2 activity and hypoglycosylation and supported graded PMM2 knockdown.

papers.title: β-Glucose-1,6-Bisphosphate Stabilizes Pathological Phophomannomutase2 Mutants In Vitro and Represents a Lead Compound to Develop Pharmacological Chaperones for the Most Common Disorder of Glycosylation, PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The study identifies β-glucose-1,6-bisphosphate as a lead pharmacological-chaperone compound that binds, conformationally stabilizes, and thermally stabilizes wild-type and pathogenic PMM2 proteins in vitro, including F119L and V129M, while also inhibiting PMM2. It is more resistant to PMM1 hydrolysis than the natural α anomer and was tolerated by HEK-293 and Caco-2 cells, but its activity, intracellular delivery, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy in patient-derived cells or patients remain untested.
papers.why: The study experimentally demonstrates that beta-glucose-1,6-bisphosphate binds and stabilizes common PMM2 mutants, establishing a lead for pharmacological chaperone development.

papers.title: Conformational response to ligand binding in phosphomannomutase2: insights into inborn glycosylation disorder.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that α-glucose 1,6-bisphosphate binds human phosphomannomutase2 (PMM2) in two approximately equivalent orientations and induces a large open-to-closed domain rearrangement supported by computational modeling, proteolysis, chemical modification, and thermal-shift experiments. It also shows that the common inactive PMM2 R141H variant still binds the bisphosphate ligand and undergoes ligand-induced conformational change, providing a ligand-bound structural model and assay rationale for PMM2-CDG drug discovery.
papers.why: The paper reports original structural and simulation methods directly on PMM2, the causal enzyme in PMM2-CDG, and identifies ligand-binding conformations relevant to drug design.

papers.title: Clinical, biochemical and molecular phenotype of congenital disorders of glycosylation: long-term follow-up.
papers.summary: This single-center cohort of 32 patients with congenital disorders of glycosylation characterized PMM2-CDG phenotypes, biochemical abnormalities, variants, and long-term outcomes. PMM2-CDG showed early onset, elevated asialo- and disialo-transferrin, frequently low tetrasialo-transferrin, and characteristic neurological, cardiac, thyroid, renal, and connective-tissue manifestations; mannose supplementation improved clinical and biochemical findings in MPI-CDG but was not studied in PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: The study provides longitudinal biochemical outcomes in 12 patients with PMM2-CDG and demonstrates sugar supplementation in patients with mechanistically related CDG subtypes.

papers.title: Synaptic roles for phosphomannomutase type 2 in a new Drosophila congenital disorder of glycosylation disease model.
papers.summary: The paper establishes CRISPR-generated and tissue-specific RNAi Drosophila models of PMM2-CDG that reproduce reduced lifespan, movement impairment, abnormal glycosylation, neuromuscular-junction overgrowth, and altered synaptic signaling. It identifies reduced NMJ MMP2 and Wingless/Frizzled-2 trans-synaptic signaling as mechanistic links between PMM2 loss and neurological phenotypes, while reviewing mannose therapy as clinically ineffective and proposing MPI inhibition for future testing.
papers.why: This study creates and characterizes the first Drosophila PMM2-CDG model and validates it for mechanistic studies and therapeutic screening.

papers.title: Tracer metabolomics reveals the role of aldose reductase in glycosylation.
papers.summary: PMM2 deficiency is associated with increased aldose reductase activity, excess intracellular and urinary polyols, depleted mannose-1-phosphate and GDP-mannose, and abnormal glycosylation. Epalrestat rewires glucose flux away from polyol production, raises PMM2-related metabolites and glycosylation, improves metabolic and behavioral outcomes in models, and was associated with clinical and biochemical improvement in three children with PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: Epalrestat is tested in patient fibroblasts, mutant zebrafish, and treated individuals, reducing polyols, increasing GDP-mannose and glycosylation, and improving clinical and biochemical outcomes.

papers.title: Heterodimerization of Two Pathological Mutants Enhances the Activity of Human Phosphomannomutase2.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the inactive PMM2 R141H subunit promotes dimerization and increases the specific activity of the hypomorphic F119L subunit, producing a heterodimer with activity comparable to the wild-type/R141H carrier heterodimer. Nevertheless, F119L/R141H PMM2 is less stable and is present at lower abundance in patient fibroblasts, motivating—but not yet demonstrating therapeutic benefit from—pharmacological chaperones or proteostasis-modulating drugs.
papers.why: The study provides direct functional evidence in patient-genotype-representative PMM2 heterodimers supporting pharmacological chaperone or proteostasis-directed stabilization as a treatment strategy.

papers.title: Biochemical phenotype of a common disease-causing mutation and a possible therapeutic approach for the phosphomannomutase 2-associated disorder of glycosylation.
papers.summary: The study shows that the recurrent PMM2 p.F119L variant weakens PMM2 dimerization, reduces enzyme activity, and destabilizes the protein. Glc-1,6-P2, and glucose monophosphates combined with vanadate, potentiated wild-type and F119L-PMM2 activity and stability, supporting pharmacological-chaperone and intracellular-activator strategies for PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: Direct experiments in PMM2 show that ligands stabilize wild-type and mutant PMM2 and propose pharmacological strategies to restore deficient enzyme function.

papers.title: Interplay of Impaired Cellular Bioenergetics and Autophagy in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: Patient-derived PMM2-CDG fibroblasts exhibit reduced maximal and ATP-linked respiration, reduced mitochondrial complex I activity, and altered autophagy/mitophagy protein abundance and glycosylation. LC3-II abundance and phosphorylated ubiquitin showed relationships with biochemical or clinical severity markers, supporting cellular bioenergetics and autophagy as mechanistic and biomarker domains relevant to PMM2-CDG research.
papers.why: The study develops disease-relevant cellular and biochemical readouts and identifies mitochondrial dysfunction, altered autophagy, LC3-II, and sorbitol as potential pharmacodynamic or severity biomarkers.

papers.title: Liver manifestations in a cohort of 39 patients with congenital disorders of glycosylation: pin-pointing the characteristics of liver injury and proposing recommendations for follow-up.
papers.summary: This cohort study characterizes liver involvement in PMM2-CDG and other congenital disorders of glycosylation, finding age-dependent aminotransferase elevations, predominantly hepatocellular injury, and PMM2-CDG liver biopsies showing glycogen deposition, steatosis, fibrosis, or cirrhosis. It recommends systematic liver follow-up with clinical examination, aminotransferase testing, liver ultrasound, and elastography, and reports variable responses to disease-specific monosaccharide therapies in related CDG types.
papers.why: Characterized liver injury patterns and proposed laboratory, ultrasound, and elastography surveillance for CDG, with substantial data from PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 26 patients with PMM2-CDG, variants affecting PMM2 folding or stabilization—especially p.Cys241Ser—were associated with lower Nijmegen severity scores and milder clinical courses, whereas p.Pro113Leu and p.Phe119Leu variants affecting the dimerization domain were associated with higher scores, more severe disease, and increased gastric feeding-tube use. Non-functioning PMM2 alleles alone did not significantly predict severity, but the small subgroup sizes, especially the three patients with p.Cys241Ser, limit certainty.
papers.why: A 26-patient cohort validates use of the NPCRS for severity assessment and identifies variant-specific genotype-phenotype relationships relevant to prognosis.

papers.title: Synergistic use of glycomics and single-molecule molecular inversion probes for identification of congenital disorders of glycosylation type-1.
papers.summary: Plasma N-glycan profiling identified glycomic patterns and glycan-ratio combinations that can stratify PMM2-CDG with other CDG-I and hereditary fructose intolerance defects, although no single reported marker was specific for PMM2-CDG. When glycomics-guided candidate-gene selection was followed by targeted smMIP sequencing, the combined workflow resolved the genetic diagnosis in 28 of 36 previously unsolved CDG-I cases (78%), including patients subsequently identified as having PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: The study develops and validates a glycomics-plus-targeted-sequencing workflow for identifying CDG-I variants in a large cohort that includes genetically defined cases.

papers.title: Spontaneous improvement of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin in PMM2-CDG without mannose observed in CDG natural history study.
papers.summary: A retrospective analysis of 37 untreated patients with PMM2-CDG found spontaneous decreases in abnormal transferrin glycosylation ratios, including seven patients with improvements similar to those reported as mannose responders and four with at least one normal test. These findings and methodological limitations of the cited mannose study undermine transferrin as a clinical-efficacy endpoint and reinforce the need for prospective natural-history studies and outcome-linked biomarkers; acetazolamide and several other experimental approaches are identified as more promising but not definitively established treatments.
papers.why: The report directly assesses transferrin glycosylation as a PMM2-CDG treatment outcome and documents spontaneous changes that affect trial interpretation.

papers.title: Dietary mannose supplementation in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This retrospective study reports that long-term oral mannose supplementation improved transferrin and other glycoprotein glycosylation in 12 of 20 patients with PMM2-CDG, with biochemical effects diminishing after treatment withdrawal. The study found no severe adverse effects or significant genotype-response relationship, but clinical outcomes were not systematically assessed and require confirmation in a controlled randomized trial.
papers.why: This retrospective study reports improved protein glycosylation in most of 20 patients with PMM2-CDG receiving long-term dietary mannose, although controlled efficacy testing remains needed.

papers.title: Unsuccessful intravenous D-mannose treatment in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: In a severely affected infant with compound-heterozygous PMM2 variants, five months of continuous intravenous D-mannose at 0.8 g/kg/day produced neither biochemical correction of N-glycosylation nor clinical improvement. The paper also reviews short-term human failures, positive fibroblast and mouse-model results, and published acetazolamide data suggesting improvement of cerebellar syndrome in PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: A five-month intravenous D-mannose trial in a patient with PMM2-CDG directly evaluates an existing dietary or metabolic therapy and reports biochemical and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Yeast Models of Phosphomannomutase 2 Deficiency, a Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
papers.summary: The study establishes yeast strains expressing orthologous SEC53 or human PMM2 patient variants as quantitative models of PMM2-CDG, with growth severity generally tracking residual phosphomannomutase activity. A 2,560-compound screen identified alpha-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid, 2’-2’-bisepigallocatechin digallate, and suramin hexasodium as allele- and genotype-dependent suppressors of yeast growth defects, but their efficacy in PMM2-CDG patients remains untested.
papers.why: Built genotype-matched yeast patient avatars and a 2,560-compound screen with quantitative enzymatic validation suitable for PMM2-CDG drug discovery.

papers.title: D-galactose supplementation in individuals with PMM2-CDG: results of a multicenter, open label, prospective pilot clinical trial.
papers.summary: An 18-week, open-label pilot trial found that oral D-galactose did not produce statistically significant clinical or biochemical improvement across nine patients with PMM2-CDG, although milder patients showed individual neurological and quality-of-life benefits. The authors proposed further placebo-controlled studies and noted that the Nijmegen Pediatric CDG rating scale may miss clinically relevant improvements.
papers.why: Prospectively tested D-galactose in nine PMM2-CDG patients, finding no significant overall benefit but possible improvement in milder cases and a trend toward improved glycosylation.

papers.title: A quantitative assessment of the evolution of cerebellar syndrome in children with phosphomannomutase-deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: In this prospective observational study of children with PMM2-CDG, International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) scores improved over 20–34 months, indicating stabilization or mild improvement of cerebellar functions despite progressive cerebellar volume loss. ICARS correlated with cerebellar volume in a small subgroup, supporting its use as a follow-up outcome measure for paediatric PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: Prospective longitudinal data support ICARS as a sensitive measure of cerebellar progression and for evaluating PMM2-CDG therapies.

papers.title: O-GlcNAcylation modulates expression and abundance of N-glycosylation machinery in an inherited glycosylation disorder.
papers.summary: Matheny-Rabun et al. used pmm2m/m mutant zebrafish to show that PMM2 deficiency is associated with increased UDP-HexNAc, increased protein O-GlcNAcylation, and compensatory induction of rate-limiting N-glycosylation proteins, especially NgBR and Dpagt1. Pharmacological and genetic perturbation experiments indicate that O-GlcNAcylation-mediated elevation of NgBR and Dpagt1 is protective against cartilage pathology, whereas epalrestat improves cartilage morphology while reducing UDP-HexNAc, O-GlcNAcylation, and NgBR/Dpagt1 abundance; the proposed human disease mechanism remains unconfirmed in patients.
papers.why: Using a PMM2-CDG zebrafish model, the study identifies O-GlcNAc-regulated N-glycosylation machinery as a disease-modifying mechanism and tests pathway modulation in vivo.

papers.title: GPI-anchor and GPI-anchored protein expression in PMM2-CDG patients.
papers.summary: In blood cells from 12 patients with PMM2-CDG, PMM2 mutations did not measurably impair GPI-anchor or most GPI-anchored protein expression, but reduced antibody recognition of neutrophil CD16 and monocyte CD14 was age-dependent or antibody-dependent. The findings indicate that abnormal glycosylation can create false-positive protein-deficiency results, while older patients show stabilization of glycosylation defects and a characteristic transferrin glycoform profile remains detectable.
papers.why: The study provides assays and data showing that abnormal immune-receptor glycosylation can alter antibody binding in PMM2-CDG, warning against incorrect interpretation of apparent protein deficiency.

papers.title: rhIGF-1 Therapy for Growth Failure and IGF-1 Deficiency in Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation Ia (PMM2 Deficiency).
papers.journal: J Investig Med High Impact Case Rep
papers.summary: In a 3-year-old boy with PMM2-CDG, recombinant human insulin-like growth factor 1 improved linear growth, with height SDS increasing from −2.73 to −1.39 over 21 months, while serum IGF-1 also increased. The case provides evidence that IGF-1 deficiency contributes to growth failure in PMM2-CDG, but the single-patient design, one asymptomatic hypoglycemic episode, and uncertain contribution to improvement in hepatopathy and protein-losing enteropathy limit the conclusions.
papers.why: This case reports substantial improvement in linear growth and IGF-related laboratory measures after recombinant human IGF-1 treatment in a child with PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Evolutionary rescue of phosphomannomutase deficiency in yeast models of human disease.
papers.summary: Experimental evolution of humanized yeast identified PGM1 mutations and an ALG9 mutation that compensate for growth and protein N-linked glycosylation defects caused by the PMM2-CDG-associated sec53-V238M allele. Biochemical reconstitution showed that reduced, but not eliminated, Pgm1 activity is optimal, while increased intracellular glucose-1,6-bisphosphate was observed in selected pgm1 backgrounds.
papers.why: Evolution of yeast carrying human PMM2/SEC53 disease alleles identifies compensatory PGM1 mutations that restore glycosylation and growth, providing a mechanistically relevant screening model and therapeutic target strategy.

papers.title: Hypoglycemia in CDG patients due to PMM2 mutations: Follow up on hyperinsulinemic patients.
papers.summary: The paper finds that hypoglycemia is rarely reported in PMM2-CDG, with hyperinsulinism identified as its cause in 43% of the reported hypoglycemic patients. Diazoxide controlled glycemia in all treated hyperinsulinemic patients, but prolonged therapy was often required and one patient developed refractory hyponatremia; no genotype–phenotype correlation for hyperinsulinism was found.
papers.why: The study documents that diazoxide successfully controls hypoglycemia in seven PMM2-CDG patients with hyperinsulinism and provides follow-up outcomes for this rare complication.

papers.title: A complement C4-derived glycopeptide is a biomarker for PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a complement C4–derived Man5GlcNAc2 glycopeptide at Asn226 as a candidate diagnostic and treatment-monitoring biomarker for PMM2-CDG, detecting it in all 35 affected individuals tested, including five with normal carbohydrate-deficient transferrin results. A targeted PRM-MS assay classified a blinded set of 16 affected and 16 control samples correctly, while a single-patient observation showed lower marker abundance after six months of epalrestat treatment without establishing clinical benefit.
papers.why: Validated the C4 Man5GlcNAc2 glycopeptide as a sensitive PMM2-CDG diagnostic and monitoring biomarker, including patients with normal or age-normalized CDT results.

papers.title: Clinical and radiological correlates of activities of daily living in cerebellar atrophy caused by PMM2 mutations (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional cohort of 26 patients with PMM2-CDG, activities of daily living disability correlated with ataxia, overall disease severity, intellectual disability, peripheral neuropathy, PMM2 genotype, and cerebellar and brainstem atrophy. Mid-pons diameter was the strongest MRI-derived predictor of functional outcome, while the authors noted that the adapted activities-of-daily-living scale requires prospective validation for PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: Quantified functional disability in PMM2-CDG and identified mid-pons atrophy as a strong MRI correlate suitable for outcome stratification.

papers.title: Hemostatic defects in congenital disorders of glycosylation.
papers.summary: This review finds that PMM2-CDG is frequently associated with quantitative N-glycosylation defects and a characteristic but incompletely understood pattern of coagulation-factor deficiencies, producing marked thrombotic and bleeding susceptibility. It highlights transferrin isoform analysis, molecular testing, coagulation monitoring, and thrombin generation testing as clinically useful diagnostic or monitoring approaches, while noting the absence of specific thromboprophylaxis or treatment guidelines.
papers.why: The review establishes characteristic hemostatic abnormalities and a monitoring framework particularly relevant to thrombotic risk in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Genotype/Phenotype Relationship: Lessons From 137 Patients With PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: In 137 participants with PMM2-CDG, clinical and biochemical assessment identified genotype-dependent severity differences that were not apparent from the Nijmegen Progression CDG Rating Scale alone. In trans with severe nonfunctioning PMM2 variants, p.Cys241Ser was associated with milder disease, whereas p.Val231Met and variants in the paper's folding category were associated with more severe biochemical abnormalities; the study also identified six previously undescribed PMM2 variants.
papers.why: The 137-patient multicenter dataset provides a reusable natural-history resource, clinical outcome scale, biochemical endpoints, and genotype-phenotype analyses for PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Protease-dependent defects in N-cadherin processing drive PMM2-CDG pathogenesis.
papers.summary: The study establishes the pmm2sa10150 zebrafish line as a model of PMM2-CDG and identifies a protease-dependent pathogenic cascade linking altered N-glycosylation to impaired proconvertase and matrix metalloproteinase activity, defective N-cadherin processing, cartilage abnormalities, and loss of motility. Pharmacological proconvertase inhibition and genetic furina reduction partially restore matrix metalloproteinase activity, N-cadherin processing, and cartilage morphology, whereas sulforaphane does not improve the phenotype.
papers.why: This study provides a PMM2-CDG zebrafish model and experimentally demonstrates rescue of protease-dependent N-cadherin and cartilage defects through targeted pathway manipulation.

papers.title: Factor XII in PMM2-CDG patients: role of N-glycosylation in the secretion and function of the first element of the contact pathway.
papers.summary: In 46 patients with PMM2-CDG, plasma FXII concentrations were generally normal, but all patients had increased amounts of a homogeneous FXII glycoform lacking N-glycosylation at Asn414; these patients did not show angioedema, and the aberrant FXII activated similarly to fully glycosylated FXII. Recombinant experiments indicated that N-glycosylation at Asn230 is required for efficient FXII folding and secretion, while vascular events were associated with hypoglycosylated FXII and other markers of the general glycosylation defect rather than with FXII concentration.
papers.why: Direct PMM2-CDG data identify an abnormal Factor XII glycoform and provide assays and a recombinant model for investigating glycosylation-related hemostatic mechanisms.

papers.title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation: Prevalence, incidence and mutational spectrum in the Polish population.
papers.summary: In a Polish cohort spanning 1997–2020, PMM2-CDG was the most common molecularly confirmed congenital disorder of glycosylation and showed high mortality. Serum transferrin isoelectric focusing was a first-line diagnostic assay, but normal or slightly abnormal results could miss cases; next-generation sequencing and array comparative genomic hybridization enabled additional subtype diagnoses.
papers.why: The study applies serum transferrin IEF and molecular confirmation across a real PMM2-CDG cohort and reports the resulting population-level diagnostic and genotype resource.

papers.title: Hyperinsulinism May Be Underreported in Hypoglycemic Patients with Phosphomannomutase 2 Deficiency
papers.summary: This retrospective case series and literature review identifies hyperinsulinism as the leading documented cause of hypoglycemia in PMM2-CDG, while finding that some cases remain etiologically unresolved because clinical and laboratory data are incomplete. Diazoxide generally controlled hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, including in one patient without markedly elevated insulin, but treatment was limited by severe hyponatremia and fluid retention in one case.
papers.why: Patient data identify hyperinsulinism as a treatable cause of hypoglycemia in PMM2-CDG and show a favorable response to diazoxide even when measured insulin is not markedly elevated.

papers.title: PMM2-CDG caused by uniparental disomy: Case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report identifies PMM2-CDG in a woman with a homozygous PMM2 p.Phe119Leu (F119L; c.357C>A) variant caused by complete maternal mixed hetero/isodisomy of chromosome 16, confirmed by short tandem repeat analysis and whole exome sequencing. The findings support testing for uniparental disomy or a deletion in PMM2-CDG patients with homoallelic PMM2 variants when segregation results do not fit, because this can alter recurrence-risk counseling.
papers.why: The report demonstrates a diagnostic pathway for diagnosing adult PMM2-CDG caused by maternal chromosome 16 uniparental disomy and improving recurrence-risk counseling.

papers.title: Patient reported outcomes for phosphomannomutase 2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG): listening to what matters for the patients and health professionals.
papers.summary: This community-centric study identified the clinical manifestations of PMM2-CDG that most affect patients’ quality of life and screened 80 quality-of-life instruments for possible direct use or adaptation into a PMM2-CDG-specific questionnaire. It also reviews three potential treatments—liposome-encapsulated mannose 1-phosphate, acetazolamide, and epalrestat—and highlights the need for disease-specific, proxy-capable outcome measures to evaluate treatment benefit.
papers.why: The study identifies priority PMM2-CDG symptoms and surveys 80 reusable quality-of-life instruments that can be adapted into a disease-specific questionnaire.

papers.title: Precision genetic cellular models identify therapies protective against ER stress.
papers.summary: The study created isogenic human hTERT RPE-1 cellular models of PMM2-CDG, DPAGT1-CDG, and NGLY1-CDDG and showed that all three models exhibit increased ER stress and autophagy, with reduced proliferation and aberrant morphology. A 1049-compound cell-painting screen followed by molecular validation identified several lead compounds that alleviated ER-stress markers, restored proliferation, and corrected abnormal morphology in the PMM2F119L/− model, although no clinical efficacy was demonstrated.
papers.why: Directly tested multiple compounds in patient-relevant CDG and deglycosylation cellular models and validated rescue of ER-stress phenotypes.

papers.title: Targeted metabolomic evaluation of peripheral blood mononucleated cells from patients with PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: Targeted HPLC metabolomics of PBMCs from seven patients with PMM2-CDG identified widespread disturbances in nucleotide-sugar, energy, antioxidant, nitrosative-stress, and free-amino-acid metabolism compared with ten healthy controls. PBMCs provided a relatively low-invasiveness cellular model for studying PMM2-CDG metabolism and monitoring therapeutic or dietary interventions, although findings may not generalize across cell types or to other tissues.
papers.why: The study identifies a broad PMM2-CDG metabolic signature in patient PBMCs and establishes a relatively low-invasiveness cellular system for glycosylation and metabolic research.

papers.title: AAV9-based PMM2 gene replacement augments PMM2 expression and improves glycosylation in primary fibroblasts of patients with phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept in vitro study found that AAV9-based PMM2 gene replacement increased PMM2 protein abundance and enzymatic activity in fibroblasts from two patients with PMM2-CDG and increased the expression of the glycoproteins ICAM-1 and LAMP1, indicating improved glycosylation. Mannose supplementation did not improve AAV infection efficiency, and the fibroblast model does not reproduce the liver and neurological manifestations of PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: This proof-of-concept study directly demonstrates AAV9-PMM2 gene replacement increasing PMM2 expression and improving glycosylation in patient fibroblasts.

papers.title: Anesthetic management of a child with phosphomannomutase-2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This single pediatric case report describes safe perioperative management of a 17-month-old boy with PMM2-CDG, muscular hypotonia, and hepatic dysfunction using rocuronium under train-of-four neuromuscular monitoring, followed by sugammadex and uneventful extubation. The observed recovery and absence of complications suggest nearly normal susceptibility to nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agents in this patient, but the authors explicitly state that further study is needed.
papers.why: This same-disease case demonstrates a concrete anesthetic management protocol using neuromuscular monitoring and sugammadex without postoperative complications.

papers.title: Evaluation of Cell Models to Study Monocyte Functions in PMM2 Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation.
papers.summary: This paper characterizes monocyte phenotype and function in PMM2-CDG patients and compares two THP-1 monocyte models that impair glycosylation. PMM2 knockdown THP-1 cells better avoided the severe ER-stress and phagocytosis effects seen with tunicamycin and more closely resembled primary PMM2-CDG monocytes, but neither model fully recapitulated the increased Candida albicans uptake observed in patients.
papers.why: Direct comparisons identify PMM2-knockdown THP-1 cells as a disease-relevant monocyte model and provide assays for surface glycosylation and phagocytic function.

papers.title: A Participatory Framework for Plain Language Clinical Management Guideline Development.
papers.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
papers.summary: This observational participatory study found that PMM2-CDG families and professionals considered clinical management guidelines valuable but reported low family awareness, jargon-related communication barriers, and a need for plain-language resources. The authors co-created a health literacy-based framework and a plain-language PMM2-CDG clinical management guideline, together with complementary resources and digital dissemination methods that may be transferable to other rare diseases.
papers.why: The study uses PMM2-CDG families and professionals to develop and evaluate a participatory framework and a plain-language clinical management guideline.

papers.title: A liposomal carbohydrate vaccine, adjuvanted with an NKT cell agonist, induces rapid and enhanced immune responses and antibody class switching.
papers.summary: A reformulated DOPC liposome carrying the ALG1-CDG/PMM2-CDG tetrasaccharide biomarker 4S and the NKT-cell agonist PBS57 elicited faster, stronger IgG responses in mice than prior formulations, including increased IgG-to-IgM switching and a predominantly IgG2b response. The resulting tetrasaccharide-specific antibodies and their ELISA detection were proposed as components of rapid diagnostic methods for ALG1-CDG and PMM2-CDG, but they were not validated in patient samples.
papers.why: The optimized liposomal vaccine induced class-switched antibodies against a PMM2-CDG-specific carbohydrate biomarker, providing a reusable platform for diagnostic reagent development.

papers.title: Untangling adaptive functioning of PMM2-CDG across age and its impact on parental stress: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 37 people with PMM2-CDG found marked deficits in adaptive functioning, especially daily living skills, communication, domestic task performance, and coping skills, without a demonstrated age-related decline or significant sex differences across the sampled groups. Greater disease severity, epilepsy, lipodystrophy, and inverted nipples were associated with poorer adaptive scores, while motor cerebellar dysfunction and behavioral problems were associated with greater parental stress, supporting standardized monitoring of adaptive, behavioral, and family functioning outcomes.
papers.why: This study validates disease-relevant adaptive, behavioral, cerebellar, quality-of-life, and parental-stress assessment tools for PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Cysteine Pathogenic Variants of PMM2 Are Sensitive to Environmental Stress with Loss of Structural Stability.
papers.summary: The study shows that the PMM2 cysteine variants C9Y and C241S destabilize PMM2, alter its secondary and tertiary structure, increase susceptibility to thermal and oxidative aggregation, and reduce cell growth while increasing apoptosis in HEK293T cells. Celastrol did not restore mutant PMM2 protein levels or provide protective effects for these variants under the tested oxidative-stress conditions.
papers.why: The study directly tests celastrol against PMM2 variants using biochemical, cellular, and computational methods relevant to PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: A PMM2-CDG caused by an A108V mutation associated with a heterozygous 70 kilobases deletion case report.
papers.summary: This case report identifies a novel compound-heterozygous PMM2-CDG genotype comprising the PMM2 c.323C>T (p.Ala108Val/A108V) variant and a maternal 70,453-bp deletion encompassing six PMM2 exons. Transferrin isoelectrofocusing, sequencing, quantitative PCR, and whole genome sequencing supported diagnosis and showed that whole genome sequencing resolved apparent variant homozygosity by detecting the deletion.
papers.why: The case provides concrete diagnostic evidence that combining transferrin testing, sequencing, copy-number analysis, and whole-genome sequencing resolves a complex PMM2 genotype.

papers.title: <i>In Silico</i> Analysis of Phosphomannomutase-2 Dimer Interface Stability and Heterodimerization with Phosphomannomutase-1.
papers.summary: This computational study supports the structural and energetic viability of PMM1/PMM2 heterodimers and identifies PMM2 dimer-interface integrity as a possible determinant of PMM2-CDG pathogenesis. It predicts destabilization by known and potentially unrecognized interface variants, but it does not experimentally validate heterodimer formation, pathogenicity, or function in vivo.
papers.why: The study provides an experimentally testable structural workflow for prioritizing PMM2 interface variants and evaluating potentially stabilizing PMM2-PMM1 heterodimers.

papers.title: 24-Week Study to Assess the PD, Safety, Tolerability, and PK of GLM101 in Participants With PMM2-CDG
papers.summary: This is a Phase 2, randomized, open-label, 24-week treatment study to evaluate the potential pharmacodynamic (PD) activity, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of GLM101 in adult, adolescent, and pediatric, patients with a confirmed diagnosis of PMM2-CDG. The planned doses of GLM101 to be investigated are 10, 20, and 30 mg/kg. The study will consist of a Screening Period, a 24-week (6-month) Treatment Period, and a 30-day (1-month) Follow-Up Period.

papers.title: Acetazolamide Efficacy in Ataxia in PMM2-CDG
papers.summary:
Objective 1 (Primary): To determine the efficacy of acetazolamide in improving ataxia in patients with PMM2-CDG.

Objective 2 (Secondary): To evaluate for any adverse events related to longer term acetazolamide administration.

Objective 3 (Secondary): To examine the effect of acetazolamide on PMM2 biomarkers including carbohydrate deficient transferrin results, electrolytes (Na, K, Cl, CO2), VBG (pH, pCO2, PO2, CO2, Base excess), liver function tests (AST, ALT, GGT, indirect and direct bilirubin, total protein, albumin, alkaline phosphatase), kidney function tests (BUN, Creatinine, Urinalysis

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Weekly Doses of GLM101 in Participants With PMM2-CDG
papers.summary:
This study is evaluating the safety, effectiveness, and how the body absorbs, distributes, and eliminates GLM101, for participants with PMM2-CDG, including children, adolescents, and adults. Researchers will compare participants receiving GLM101 to those receiving a placebo to see if GLM101 improves symptoms of PMM2-CDG.

The study includes two treatment parts: a 24-week double blind placebo-controlled treatment period (Part A), and a 24-week open-label phase where every participant will receive GLM101(Part B).

papers.title: Open-Label Extension Study to Assess GLM101 in PMM2-CDG Patients
papers.summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to provide continued access to GLM101 to treat PMM2-CDG in people who have previously received GLM101 in other trials and learn about the long term effect of GLM101. Participants will complete weekly infusions of GLM101 at the same dose level received in previous trials.

papers.title: Oral Epalrestat Therapy in Pediatric Subjects With PMM2-CDG
papers.summary: This is a prospective, single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to assess the safety, tolerability, and clinical and metabolic improvement of pediatric subjects with PMM2-CDG on oral epalrestat therapy vs. placebo.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation
Genotypes and phenotypes of patients in the UK with carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type 1.
papers.summary: The study identifies biallelic PMM2 variants as a cause of carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type 1a and shows that affected patients have deficient phosphomannomutase activity. Residual phosphomannomutase activity, PMM2 genotype, and the typical type 1 transferrin profile were not correlated with disease severity.
papers.why: The study provides disease-specific diagnostic and genotype-phenotype data for PMM2-CDG, but does not evaluate a new therapeutic solution.

papers.title: High conformational flexibility of phosphomannomutase 2: Implications for functioning mechanisms, stability and pharmacological chaperone design
papers.summary: Structural and molecular-dynamics studies of human and murine phosphomannomutase 2 indicate that PMM2 is a highly flexible enzyme involved in the N-glycosylation pathway, with conformational motions relevant to substrate binding, intermediate reorientation, and product release. The findings identify enzyme-state stabilization by pharmacological chaperones as a proposed therapeutic design strategy, but no chaperone intervention was tested.

papers.title: Enzymatic Production of β-Glucose 1,6-Bisphosphate Through Manipulation of Catalytic Magnesium Coordination
papers.summary: The paper describes an in vitro strategy using a β-phosphoglucomutase variant to efficiently synthesize anomer-specific β-glucose 1,6-bisphosphate, followed by an environmentally considerate precipitation purification step. β-Glucose 1,6-bisphosphate had previously been proposed as a treatment for PMM2-related congenital disorder of glycosylation, but this study does not report restoration of phosphomannomutase activity or testing in patients or disease models.

papers.title: Founder mutation in the PMM2 promotor causes hyperinsulinemic hypoglycaemia/polycystic kidney disease (HIPKD).
papers.summary: The study identifies a shared 0.312 Mb haplotype around the PMM2 promoter variant c.-167G>T in 11 patients with polycystic kidney disease with hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia (HIPKD) from seven unrelated European families, supporting a founder effect. The variant is associated with reduced or organ-specific PMM2 expression and may cause kidney and pancreatic beta-cell disease, while PMM2 coding variants cause PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation type 1a.

papers.title: Kinetic mechanism and pH dependence of the kinetic parameters of Pseudomonas aeruginosa phosphomannomutase/phosphoglucomutase.
papers.summary: The study characterizes phosphomannomutase activity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa phosphomannomutase/phosphoglucomutase, showing that a Ser108 phosphorylation-site mutation redirects phosphorylation and reduces activity approximately 20-fold while preserving substantial catalytic function. It also identifies inhibition of this enzyme as a possible antibacterial strategy and resolves substrate inhibition, catalytic residues, and pH-dependent kinetic behavior, but it does not test candidate inhibitors in cells or animals.

papers.title: Mammalian phosphomannomutase PMM1 is the brain IMP-sensitive glucose-1,6-bisphosphatase.
papers.summary: The study identifies PMM1 as the IMP-sensitive brain glucose-1,6-bisphosphatase responsible for degrading glucose 1,6-bisphosphate in brain. Recombinant PMM1 showed strong IMP stimulation of bisphosphatase activity, PMM1 transfection lowered glucose 1,6-bisphosphate in HEK293T cells, and PGM2L1 transfection increased it; wild-type mouse brain glucose 1,6-bisphosphate decreased after ischemia, whereas PMM1-deficient brain was unchanged.

papers.title: Remodeling the proteostasis network to rescue glucocerebrosidase variants by inhibiting ER-associated degradation and enhancing ER folding.
papers.summary: In fibroblasts from patients with Gaucher disease, combined lacidipine and Eeyarestatin I increased native folding, lysosomal trafficking, and activity of the destabilized L444P glucocerebrosidase variant while reducing apoptosis associated with ERAD inhibition. The study provides a proteostasis-modulation strategy for rescuing unstable, degradation-prone proteins, but it did not test PMM2 variants or the PMM2 protein stability mechanism.

papers.title: A counterintuitive approach to treat enzyme deficiencies: use of enzyme inhibitors for restoring mutant enzyme activity.
papers.summary: The review describes active-site-specific chaperones as competitive enzyme inhibitors that can be used at sub-inhibitory concentrations to assist folding of misfolded enzymes, prevent excessive endoplasmic-reticulum-associated degradation, and restore enzyme activity in lysosomal storage disorders. It does not mention PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation or the specific mechanism “PMM2 protein stability,” so it provides only a general pharmacological-chaperone strategy rather than disease-specific evidence for that mechanism.

papers.title: Glycerol increases the yield and activity of human phenylalanine hydroxylase mutant enzymes produced in a prokaryotic expression system.
papers.summary: In recombinant human phenylalanine hydroxylase produced in a prokaryotic system, glycerol increased the yield of soluble wild-type and R270K or V388M mutant proteins by approximately 2- to 3-fold and increased the purified enzymes' specific activity. These findings support chemical-chaperone-mediated protein stabilization as a possible strategy for conformational diseases, but the proposed therapeutic effect was speculative and was not tested in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Folding and activity of mutant cystathionine β-synthase depends on the position and nature of the purification tag: characterization of the R266K CBS mutant.
papers.summary: The study shows that the R266K cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) mutant is misfolded and thermally less stable than wild type, with altered heme/PLP-related function. Replacing a bulky GST fusion partner with a small C-terminal 6xHis tag restored active tetramer formation and approximately 65% wild-type activity, whereas chemical chaperones did not significantly improve activity. These data support purification-tag engineering as a way to stabilize and characterize a misfolded enzyme, but the paper does not study PMM2 or directly test PMM2 protein stability.

papers.title: A sensitive fluorescence-based assay for monitoring GM2 ganglioside hydrolysis in live patient cells and their lysates.
papers.summary: The paper reports a fluorescence-based assay for measuring GM2 ganglioside hydrolysis in live cells and lysates. In adult Tay-Sachs fibroblasts pre-treated with the pharmacological chaperone Pyrimethamine, mutant beta-hexosaminidase A levels and substrate hydrolysis increased relative to mock-treated cells; the paper does not study PMM2 protein stability or PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: The Chaperoning Activity of Amino-oxyacetic Acid on Folding-Defective Variants of Human Alanine:Glyoxylate Aminotransferase Causing Primary Hyperoxaluria Type I.
papers.summary: The study provides proof-of-principle that amino-oxyacetic acid can act as a pharmacological chaperone for folding-defective human alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase variants causing Primary Hyperoxaluria Type I. It increases AGT thermal stability, reduces intracellular aggregation of one variant, and promotes correct peroxisomal import of two variants.
