papers.title: Epalrestat Alleviates Reactive Oxygen Species and Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress by Maintaining Glycosylation in IMS32 Schwann Cells Under Exposure to Galactosemic Conditions.
papers.summary: In galactosemic IMS32 Schwann cells, ranirestat reduced galactitol accumulation, whereas low-dose epalrestat did not; both drugs reduced ROS production, ER stress, and glycolytic impairment, but neither restored mitochondrial membrane potential or morphology. Epalrestat uniquely reduced aberrant RCA120-binding glycosylation, and cited PMM2-CDG studies report that epalrestat improves PMM2 activity and glycosylation in PMM2 mutant worms and patient-derived fibroblasts.

papers.title: Drug screening identifies aldose reductase as a novel target for treating cisplatin-induced hearing loss.
papers.summary: The paper identifies aldose reductase as a mediator of cisplatin-induced cochlear injury and as a target for otoprotection. Tiliroside and the approved aldose reductase inhibitor Epalrestat reduced oxidative stress and cell death and protected hearing function in the studied cisplatin models.

papers.title: Targeting <i>aldose reductase</i> using natural African compounds as promising agents for managing diabetic complications.
papers.summary: This computational study identified five African natural compounds—(+)-pipoxide, Zinc000095485961, Naamidine A, (−)-pipoxide, and 1,6-di-o-p-hydroxybenzoyl-beta-d-glucopyranoside—as candidate aldose reductase inhibitors using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, activity prediction, 100 ns molecular dynamics, and MM-PBSA. Their aldose reductase binding and inhibitory potential were stronger than benchmarked standard inhibitors in several computational analyses, but no in vitro or in vivo confirmation was performed, and PASS predicted no aldose reductase inhibition for either pipoxide enantiomer or Naamidine A.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Identification and Evaluation of Epalrestat and Ranirestat-Like Compounds Against Aldose Reductase: Therapeutic Management of Diabetic Neuropathy.
papers.summary: This computational study identifies PubChem CID:45110135 and PubChem CID:58643777 as epalrestat- and ranirestat-like candidates predicted to bind and inhibit aldose reductase. Docking, ADMET, PASS, and 500 ns molecular-dynamics analyses suggested favorable interactions, predicted safety and antineuropathic activity, and preservation of aldose-reductase structural stability, but the study did not perform in vitro or in vivo validation.

papers.title: Plumbagin Protects Diabetogenic Cataract Formation by Mitigating Lens Aldose Reductase and Oxidative Stress.
papers.summary: Plumbagin inhibited lens aldose reductase and reduced oxidative stress in isolated goat lenses exposed to high glucose, preventing lens opacity and preserving lens protein content in an ex vivo diabetic-cataract model. The study provides an experimentally supported aldose-reductase-directed intervention, but its effects were limited to in vitro, in silico, and ex vivo systems and require validation in vivo.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Aldose Reductase and Isoxazole Derivatives: An In Vitro and In Silico Approach to Its Correlation With Diabetic Conditions.
papers.summary: The paper reports that isoxazole and eight derivatives inhibit aldose reductase in vitro, with several compounds more potent than epalrestat, and molecular docking supports binding within its active site. These results identify experimental aldose-reductase inhibitors and computational lead-design methods, but no compound was tested in animals or patients with PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Metformin-stimulated mannose transport in dermal fibroblasts.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a metformin-stimulated, mannose-selective transport activity in dermal fibroblasts and shows that metformin, particularly with mannose, restores lipid-linked oligosaccharide synthesis and protein N-glycosylation in PMM2-CDG/type Ia fibroblasts. It also detects the transport activity in type Ia and type Ib congenital disorder of glycosylation fibroblasts, supporting its use as a potential mechanism-based therapy.

papers.title: A zebrafish model of congenital disorders of glycosylation with phosphomannose isomerase deficiency reveals an early opportunity for corrective mannose supplementation.
papers.summary: The paper establishes an Mpi-deficient zebrafish model of MPI-CDG with reduced mannose-6-phosphate, lipid-linked oligosaccharides, protein N-glycosylation, survival, and organ development. Early mannose supplementation rescued the model’s biochemical and morphological defects, while delayed treatment did not, supporting transfer of the mechanism to disorders such as PMM2-CDG but not establishing clinical efficacy in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Mannose metabolism normalizes gut homeostasis by blocking the TNF-α-mediated proinflammatory circuit.
papers.summary: The paper reports that mannose supplementation ameliorates colitis and promotes recovery by normalizing protein N-glycosylation in intestinal epithelial cells, thereby preserving epithelial integrity and reducing macrophage inflammatory activation. It also identifies reduced glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate-mediated translational suppression of TNF-α by mannose and shows that epalrestat activation of PMM2 further sensitizes colitis to mannose.

papers.title: The relative contribution of mannose salvage pathways to glycosylation in PMI-deficient mouse embryonic fibroblast cells.
papers.summary: The study shows that PMI-deficient mouse embryonic fibroblasts can support N-glycosylation through mannose salvage from endogenous and external glycoconjugates. Blocking lysosomal or endosomal pathways reduces glycosylation, while adding mannose restores it, identifying mannose availability as a potential intervention point for deficient N-glycosylation.

papers.title: Oral D-mannose therapy during pregnancy in a woman with MPI-CDG: A case report and management review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a pregnant woman with MPI-CDG in whom oral D-mannose was discontinued at 6 weeks' gestation because of possible fetal toxicity, after which severe digestive symptoms and hypoglycemia relapsed. D-mannose was restarted at 10 weeks' gestation, rapidly resolving symptoms, and transferrin glycoform and coagulation monitoring supported gradual dose escalation through delivery; the authors suggest low-dose D-mannose may be a safe option during pregnancy, although human teratogenicity data were unavailable.

papers.title: Variation of the serum N-glycosylation during the pregnancy of a MPI-CDG patient.
papers.summary: In one pregnant patient with MPI-CDG, withdrawal of D-mannose was followed by a transient improvement in protein N-glycosylation, measured by lower carbohydrate-deficient transferrin, reduced abnormal transferrin glycoforms, and increased triantennary serum N-glycans. The findings support carbohydrate-deficient transferrin testing, transferrin isoelectrofocusing, and serum N-glycome analysis as mechanistically relevant assays, while D-mannose is a reported therapy for MPI-CDG that acts upstream of protein N-glycosylation.

unread.title: International clinical guidelines for the management of phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorders of glycosylation: Diagnosis, treatment and follow up.
unread.why: This systematic guideline provides disease-specific clinical evaluation, management, and follow-up recommendations for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Sorbitol Is a Severity Biomarker for PMM2-CDG with Therapeutic Implications.
unread.why: The study tests epalrestat in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts and a patient while providing sorbitol, glycoproteomics, and disease-severity measures for monitoring response.

unread.title: High residual activity of PMM2 in patients' fibroblasts: possible pitfall in the diagnosis of CDG-Ia (phosphomannomutase deficiency).
unread.why: The study identifies a diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates that leukocyte PMM2 measurement combined with PMM2 mutation analysis improves detection of mild CDG-Ia.

unread.title: A broad spectrum of clinical presentations in congenital disorders of glycosylation I: a series of 26 cases.
unread.why: The cohort establishes transferrin-based laboratory testing and clinical outcome characterization for PMM2-CDG and reports successful mannose treatment in the related CDG-Ib subtype.

unread.title: The Effects of PMM2-CDG-Causing Mutations on the Folding, Activity, and Stability of the PMM2 Protein.
unread.why: Functional analysis of patient-derived and murine PMM2 mutants shows that several destabilizing variants retain activity and identifies protein-folding rescue as a concrete therapeutic strategy.

unread.title: A nationwide survey of PMM2-CDG in Italy: high frequency of a mild neurological variant associated with the L32R mutation.
unread.why: The nationwide cohort reports validated transferrin glycoform analysis and links the L32R genotype and biochemical underglycosylation to a distinct mild PMM2-CDG phenotype.

unread.title: Coagulation abnormalities in a prospective cohort of 50 patients with PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation.
unread.why: A prospective 50-patient cohort establishes anticoagulant biomarkers and longitudinal clinical outcomes for bleeding, thrombosis, antithrombin deficiency, and stroke-like episodes in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Instrumented assessment of gait disturbance in PMM2-CDG adults: a feasibility analysis.
unread.why: Demonstrated that instrumented gait analysis quantifies gait impairment and correlates with clinical severity in adults with PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Mild clinical and biochemical phenotype in two patients with PMM2-CDG (congenital disorder of glycosylation Ia).
unread.why: Showed that sensitive quantitative transferrin glycoform analysis can detect PMM2-CDG missed by routine or nearly normalized conventional screening.

unread.title: Insight on molecular pathogenesis and pharmacochaperoning potential in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency, provided by novel human phosphomannomutase 2 structures.
unread.why: Resolved complete PMM2 structures with ligand-bound states and classified patient variants to identify folding- and dimerization-defective alleles potentially amenable to pharmacochaperoning.

unread.title: A functional platform for the selection of pathogenic variants of PMM2 amenable to rescue via the use of pharmacological chaperones.
unread.why: The study directly characterizes multiple PMM2-CDG variants and shows that compound VIII restores thermal stability to unstable mutant PMM2 proteins while providing a reusable variant-assessment platform.

unread.title: Liver transplantation recovers hepatic N-glycosylation with persistent IgG glycosylation abnormalities: Three-year follow-up in a patient with phosphomannomutase-2-congenital disorder of glycosylation.
unread.why: Three-year follow-up provides direct patient evidence that liver transplantation improves growth, neurodevelopment, liver function, coagulation, and the type I transferrin profile in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Beneficial effects of Glc-1,6-P<sub>2</sub> modulation on mutant phosphomannomutase-2.
unread.why: In patient-derived fibroblasts, increasing glucose-1,6-bisphosphate improved glycosylation and LAMP1, PTX3, and lysosomal-enzyme biomarkers while supporting the metabolite as a candidate therapy.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia in a Chinese family: Function analysis of a novel PMM2 complex heterozygosis mutation.
unread.why: The study experimentally quantifies the functional deficit of a novel PMM2 complex-heterozygous mutation and demonstrates a transferable workflow for variant interpretation.

unread.title: Mutations in PMM2 that cause congenital disorders of glycosylation, type Ia (CDG-Ia).
unread.why: The study created a broad PMM2 variant catalog and online database useful for variant interpretation and genetic diagnosis of PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Targeted disruption of the mouse phosphomannomutase 2 gene causes early embryonic lethality.
unread.why: Targeted Pmm2 disruption generated an in vivo PMM2-CDG model, although the homozygous null genotype causes early embryonic lethality.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia (CDG-Ia): phenotypic spectrum of the R141H/F119L genotype.
unread.why: The 25-patient longitudinal series defines genotype-specific clinical courses and measurable growth, neurological, and neuroimaging outcomes for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Expression analysis revealing destabilizing mutations in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG): expression analysis of PMM2-CDG mutations.
unread.why: The paper functionally classifies pathogenic PMM2 variants and provides assays and mechanistic evidence supporting stabilization of misfolded mutants with pharmacological chaperones.

unread.title: Functional significance of PMM2 mutations in mildly affected patients with congenital disorders of glycosylation Ia.
unread.why: The study measures mutation-dependent PMM activity in patient fibroblasts and a yeast expression system, providing a functional assay for PMM2 variants.

unread.title: Long-term evolution of eight Spanish patients with CDG type Ia: typical and atypical manifestations.
unread.why: Eight patients were followed long term to establish the age-dependent morbidity, survival, neurological outcomes, and post-infancy stability of PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Biochemical and molecular studies in 26 Spanish patients with congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia.
unread.why: The study supplies a molecular diagnostic workflow and population-specific PMM2 variant catalog supporting routine screening and diagnosis of PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: A new insight into PMM2 mutations in the French population.
unread.why: Functional testing of novel recombinant PMM2 variants and haplotype characterization provide directly reusable diagnostic and variant-classification resources for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Neural and metabolic dysregulation in PMM2-deficient human in vitro neural models.
unread.why: The paper establishes disease-relevant iPSC-derived neuronal and cortical-organoid models with metabolic, multi-omic, and PMM2 activity measurements for mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

unread.title: Neurological presentation of a congenital disorder of glycosylation CDG-Ia: implications for diagnosis and genetic counseling.
unread.why: The study provides direct diagnostic evidence that leukocyte PMM activity can identify CDG-Ia even when fibroblast activity is intermediate.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia: heterogeneity in the clinical presentation from multivisceral failure to hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia as leading symptoms in three infants with phosphomannomutase deficiency.
unread.why: Three patients with CDG-Ia had persistent hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia that responded to diazoxide, while transferrin and PMM testing supported diagnosis.

unread.title: Neurological manifestations in PMM2-congenital disorders of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG): Insights into clinico-radiological characteristics, recommendations for follow-up, and future directions.
unread.why: This natural-history study provides PMM2-CDG outcome data and preliminary clinical evidence on acetazolamide and levetiracetam use.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type 1a in a macrosomic 16-month-old boy with an atypical phenotype and homozygosity of the N216I mutation.
unread.why: The case confirms CDG-Ia through transferrin typing, PMM activity measurement in two cell types, and identification of the N216I genotype.

unread.title: Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation in Portugal-Two Decades of Experience.
unread.why: A 63-patient cohort demonstrates a diagnostic workflow integrating transferrin testing, biochemical assays, and sequencing for PMM2-CDG and other CDGs.

unread.title: Causes of mortality in the congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: The 37-patient study provides PMM2-CDG-relevant natural-history data on mortality, pericardial effusion, neurological progression, infection, and supportive-care endpoints.

unread.title: Anthropometric Phenotype of Patients with PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: This study provides longitudinal outcome measures and genotype-associated anthropometric phenotypes for patients with PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: PMM2-CDG
unread.why: The review describes established diagnostic testing, clinical staging, and management-relevant outcome characterization specifically for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: The clinical spectrum of phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (CDG-Ia).
unread.why: This disease-specific review documents the clinical spectrum and diagnostic framework for PMM2 deficiency, providing reusable outcome and phenotyping information.

unread.title: Clinical, laboratory and molecular findings and long-term follow-up data in 96 French patients with PMM2-CDG (phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorder of glycosylation) and review of the literature.
unread.why: The large PMM2-CDG cohort provides reusable natural-history, clinical, laboratory, and follow-up outcome data with molecular characterization.

unread.title: Successful prenatal mannose treatment for congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ia in mice.
unread.why: The study directly demonstrates that prenatal mannose treatment rescues embryonic lethality in a hypomorphic Pmm2 model of PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: The X-ray crystal structures of human alpha-phosphomannomutase 1 reveal the structural basis of congenital disorder of glycosylation type 1a.
unread.why: The structures provide a disease-relevant experimental and computational framework for understanding PMM-family biology and PMM2-CDG mutation effects.

unread.title: Long-term follow-up in PMM2-CDG: are we ready to start treatment trials?
unread.why: This long-term PMM2-CDG study provides longitudinal clinical and biochemical data directly usable for selecting clinical-trial endpoints and monitoring disease course.

unread.title: Carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type IA (phosphomannomutase-deficiency).
unread.why: This PMM2-CDG review describes the established transferrin glycoform assay used for biochemical diagnosis of CDG-Ia.

unread.title: From gestalt to gene: early predictive dysmorphic features of PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: This PMM2-CDG study develops and tests facial-analysis and clinical dysmorphology tools for earlier diagnosis and severity assessment.

unread.title: Subcutaneous fat pads on body MRI--an early sign of congenital disorder of glycosylation PMM2-CDG (CDG1a).
unread.why: The case identifies an early, clinically occult MRI sign of PMM2-CDG that can support earlier diagnosis.

unread.title: Elevated oxysterol and N-palmitoyl-O-phosphocholineserine levels in congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: Shows PPCS elevation in plasma from individuals including PMM2-CDG and supports its use as a diagnostic biomarker in severe early-onset liver disease.

unread.title: Assessing the effects of PMM2 variants on protein stability.
unread.why: Provides validated computational simulations predicting structural and stability effects of PMM2 variants relevant to PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) Associated with Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Monogenic Diseases (PGT-M) in a Romanian Carrier Couple for Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation Type Ia (CDG-Ia): A Case Report.
unread.why: Reports an IVF/PGT-M workflow applied to a carrier couple at risk for PMM2-CDG, including molecular discrimination of embryos carrying pathogenic PMM2 alleles.

unread.title: Novel mouse model reveals neurodevelopmental origin of PMM2-CDG brain pathology.
unread.why: Develops a mouse model reproducing PMM2-CDG cerebellar hypoplasia, ataxia, seizures, early lethality, and brain molecular abnormalities, with human tissue corroboration.

unread.title: AAV-based gene replacement reverses Neurexin-2 downregulation in the cerebellum of a mouse model of phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG)
unread.why: Demonstrates that AAV9-mediated PMM2 gene treatment reverses PMM2-related Neurexin-2 downregulation in the mouse cerebellum.

unread.title: Hypoglycosylation lowers the mechanical activation threshold of Piezo1 and enhances cortical neuronal mechanotransduction: implications for PMM2-CDG
unread.why: Uses targeted genetic and pharmacological perturbation with electrophysiology and calcium imaging to establish how hypoglycosylation alters Piezo1 function relevant to PMM2-CDG neurological phenotypes.

unread.title: Establishing an auxin-inducible GFP nanobody-based acute protein knockdown system to mimic hypomorphic mutations during early medaka embryogenesis
unread.why: Establishes an inducible medaka system that acutely reduces Pmm2 protein and activity to patient-relevant hypomorphic levels during embryogenesis.

unread.title: In silico Analysis of PMM2 Dimer Interface Stability and Heterodimerization with PMM1
unread.why: Provides structural and interface-energy modeling to evaluate PMM2 dimerization, PMM1-PMM2 heterodimerization, and disease-associated interface mutations.

unread.title: Untangling adaptive functioning of PMM2-CDG across age and its impact on parental stress: a cross-sectional study
unread.why: The study provides validated clinical instruments and outcome measures for monitoring adaptive deficits, disease severity, behavior, and parental stress in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: A Case of PMM2-CDG Caused by an A108V Mutation Associated With a Heterozygous 70 Kilobases Deletion
unread.why: This PMM2-CDG case demonstrates a diagnostic workflow combining transferrin profiling, targeted sequencing, quantitative PCR, and whole-genome sequencing to resolve a complex PMM2 genotype.

unread.title: Cardiomyopathy, an uncommon phenotype of congenital disorders of glycosylation: Recommendations for baseline screening and follow-up evaluation.
unread.why: The multicenter study reports cardiomyopathy screening and longitudinal cardiac phenotyping in a large CDG cohort, including ten patients with PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Liposome-encapsulated mannose-1-phosphate therapy improves global N-glycosylation in different congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: The study directly tests GLM101 in PMM2-CDG patient fibroblasts and shows improved expression of mature N-glycoforms, supporting a potential glycan-restoration therapy.

unread.title: Should patients with Phosphomannomutase 2-CDG (PMM2-CDG) be screened for adrenal insufficiency?
unread.why: This PMM2-CDG natural-history study identifies adrenal insufficiency as a clinically actionable complication and supports cortisol monitoring, stimulation testing, and hormone replacement.

unread.title: Clinical severity and cardiac phenotype in phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorders of glycosylation : Insights into genetics and management recommendations.
unread.why: The large multicenter PMM2-CDG study provides natural-history cardiac endpoints, identifies a high-risk genotype, and recommends cardiac surveillance.

unread.title: AAV-based gene replacement therapy prevents and halts manifestation of abnormal neurological phenotypes in a novel mouse model of PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The paper develops a Pmm2-deficient mouse model and shows that AAV9-PMM2 gene replacement prevents and halts relevant neurological phenotypes.

unread.title: "Hide and seek": Misleading transferrin variants in PMM2-CDG complicate diagnostics.
unread.why: The study identifies misleading transferrin variants in PMM2-CDG and validates neuraminidase treatment plus orthogonal glycosylation analyses to improve diagnostic interpretation.

unread.title: Sensitivity of transferrin isoform analysis for PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: Ten years of testing data establish 94% sensitivity of transferrin isoform analysis for PMM2-CDG while defining recurrent false-positive transferrin variants.

unread.title: In vitro treatment with liposome-encapsulated Mannose-1-phosphate restores N-glycosylation in PMM2-CDG patient-derived fibroblasts.
unread.why: GLM101 normalized key metabolites and glycan abnormalities in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts and showed favorable preclinical pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and tolerability.

unread.title: Cysteine variants in PMM2 lead to protein instability and higher sensitivity to oxidative stress in PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The paper directly examines destabilizing PMM2 cysteine variants and reports partial rescue by celastrol, identifying a candidate therapeutic and model for variant-specific dysfunction.

unread.title: Exploring a Circulating miRNA Signature for PMM2-CDG: Initial Insights Toward Diagnosis, Stratification, and Monitoring.
unread.why: The study develops an initial blood-based miRNA signature that distinguished PMM2-CDG patients from controls with an XGBoost AUC of 0.917.

unread.title: Motor improvement in children with PMM2-CDG syndrome following a six-month rehabilitation treatment utilising whole-body vibration; a retrospective study.
unread.why: A six-month rehabilitation program incorporating whole-body vibration was associated with measurable motor and gait improvements in children with PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Treatment of Single Patient With PMM2-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation With Govorestat (AT-007), an Aldose Reductase Inhibitor.
unread.why: A 36-month single-patient expanded-access treatment reported tolerability of govorestat together with biochemical, coagulation, sorbitol, and clinical outcome improvements.

unread.title: HepG2 PMM2-CDG knockout model: A versatile platform for variant and therapeutic evaluation.
unread.why: The HepG2 knockout model reproduces PMM2 deficiency and altered glycoprotein patterns and is validated for evaluating PMM2 variants and candidate therapies.

unread.title: Activity values of the enzyme phosphomanomutase 2 for diagnosing the CDG Ia glycosylation defect.
unread.why: The study establishes a reference range for leukocyte PMM2 activity and demonstrates its ability to detect a PMM2-CDG patient with no residual enzymatic activity.

unread.title: Suspected Central Adrenal Insufficiency in a Patient with Phosphomannomutase 2-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
unread.why: The case demonstrates that low cortisol-binding globulin can produce misleading total-cortisol results in PMM2-CDG and supports use of salivary free cortisol to assess adrenal function.

unread.title: Lack of homozygotes for the most frequent disease allele in carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type 1A.
unread.why: The study directly tested SSCP and sequencing in 56 CDG-Ia patients, detected nearly all disease alleles, and identified genotype-phenotype associations.

unread.title: The challenge of CDG diagnosis.
unread.why: The paper provides practical diagnostic tools for CDG and specifically warns that serum transferrin testing can be falsely negative in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Interference of transferrin isoform types with carbohydrate-deficient transferrin quantification in the identification of alcohol abuse.
unread.why: Using a CDG-Ia patient and carriers, the study showed that HPLC and isoelectric focusing resolve transferrin isoforms and verify misleading CDT immunoassay results.

unread.title: Gastrointestinal and other clinical manifestations in 17 children with congenital disorders of glycosylation type Ia, Ib, and Ic.
unread.why: The patient study provides clinically observable and histological indicators prompting PMM2-CDG testing and characterizes relevant gastrointestinal and liver outcomes.

unread.title: Thrombotic complications in patients with PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The systematic review and 15-patient cohort identify actionable coagulation biomarkers, risk factors, monitoring intervals, and management measures for PMM2-CDG-associated thrombosis.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia presenting with hydrops fetalis.
unread.why: The report identifies fetal hydrops as a presentation of PMM2-CDG and proposes measuring PMM activity in chorionic villi or amniocytes for prenatal diagnosis.

unread.title: Cerebellar ataxia and congenital disorder of glycosylation Ia (CDG-Ia) with normal routine CDG screening.
unread.why: The study shows that direct PMM activity testing detects PMM2-CDG cases missed by normal or inconclusive transferrin isofocusing.

unread.title: Phosphomannose isomerase inhibitors improve N-glycosylation in selected phosphomannomutase-deficient fibroblasts.
unread.why: MLS0315771 improved N-glycosylation in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts and increased mannose flux toward glycosylation in zebrafish embryos.

unread.title: Risk assessment of acute vascular events in congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia.
unread.why: The study identifies clinical and laboratory factors associated with acute vascular events in PMM2-CDG, including young age, fever, immobilization, factor levels, and protein C abnormalities.

unread.title: Pharmacological Chaperoning: A Potential Treatment for PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: A screen of 10,000 compounds identified small molecules that stabilized mutant PMM2, increased mutant activity in cells, and provided lead structures for therapeutic development.

unread.title: Hydrophobic Man-1-P derivatives correct abnormal glycosylation in Type I congenital disorder of glycosylation fibroblasts.
unread.why: Both membrane-permeable Man-1-P derivatives restored lipid-linked oligosaccharide synthesis and protein glycosylation in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts, with compound II showing greater potency.

unread.title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) may be underdiagnosed when mimicking mitochondrial disease.
unread.why: The cases demonstrate that CDT and sialotransferrin isoelectric focusing can identify PMM2-CDG masquerading as mitochondrial disease and avoid delayed diagnosis.

unread.title: Analysis of glycosylation in CDG-Ia fibroblasts by fluorophore-assisted carbohydrate electrophoresis: implications for extracellular glucose and intracellular mannose 6-phosphate.
unread.why: FACE provides a nonradioactive assay of CDG-Ia lipid-linked oligosaccharides and experimentally identifies excess M6P-stimulated LLO cleavage as a mechanism that may underlie mannose-therapy failure.

unread.title: Characterization of two unusual truncating PMM2 mutations in two CDG-Ia patients.
unread.why: The study characterizes novel truncating PMM2 mutations and demonstrates the utility of combining genomic, transcript, and enzymatic testing for PMM2-CDG diagnosis.

unread.title: Hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia--leading symptom in a patient with congenital disorder of glycosylation Ia (phosphomannomutase deficiency).
unread.why: This PMM2-CDG case provides patient-tested management of severe hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia and establishes its molecular and biochemical diagnosis.

unread.title: Identification of intercellular cell adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) as a hypoglycosylation marker in congenital disorders of glycosylation cells.
unread.why: The paper validates ICAM-1 as a cellular glycosylation and gene-complementation readout in PMM2-CDG and shows partial correction by PMM2 complementation.
